h: How to Win (or at Least Look Like You Tried)
p: Glow bowling is all about the atmosphere, but there's still a bit of technique if you fancy beating the family show-off. Pick a ball you can swing comfortably without straining your wrist, as a lighter ball you can control will usually beat a heavy one you're wrestling with. Aim for the arrows on the lane rather than the pins, as they're closer and easier to focus on, and follow through smoothly with your arm pointing where you want the ball to go.
Under the glowing lights, the lanes and pins look fantastic, but they can also make it harder to judge distance at first. Give yourself a frame or two to adjust before you start blaming the lane.

If you're organising a birthday here, numbers matter. Six or so players per lane keeps the game moving, while bigger groups can start to drag and leave kids restless. Sort out who's on which lane before you arrive to avoid squabbles, and think about food timings so the cake doesn't clash with the final frame.

Glow bowling also suits mixed-age groups better than you might expect. Younger children are usually so taken with the glowing pins that the score hardly matters, while teenagers get a game that feels a bit cooler than the standard lanes back home.

Bowling makes a great late-afternoon or evening activity, and the location makes it easy to fit in. M&D's sits right by the M74, so it's quick to reach from Glasgow, Hamilton and the surrounding towns. After the last ball has rolled, Motherwell and Hamilton both have plenty of places for a meal, and Glasgow's city centre is close enough for anyone wanting to turn a few frames into a proper night out.
